topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, frames the lecture series, and outlines the core learning objectives concerning cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Luck, Genetics, and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational debate over what drives cancer, contrasting intrinsic biological bad luck and genetic predisposition with environmental exposures and global epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Pathogens and Viral Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on how infectious agents contribute to cancer development, highlighted by a detailed case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which chemical and physical mutagens undergo host metabolic processing to induce direct DNA damage and adducts.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Developmental Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic drivers of carcinogenesis, including tumor promoter biology, inflammatory microenvironments, and host tissue developmental susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify carcinogen exposure and verify carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes with framing remarks summarising environmental risk factors, testing challenges, and everyday risk-benefit calculations.
